title: Continuous Profiling for GPUs — Matthias Loibl, Polar Signals
talk_summary: A vendor talk on Polar Signals' continuous sampled profiling (eBPF-based, always-on, low overhead) extended to GPU metrics via NVML and CUDA kernel timing. The core transferable idea is cheap, always-on sampled measurement of where time/resources go, rather than exhaustive tracing.

takeaways.technique: Always-on sampled profiling of build hosts
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a low-overhead eBPF sampler continuously in production instead of full tracing, accepting that you miss individual events but catch the big picture over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we sample for a certain duration like 10 seconds and we uh only sample 100 times per second
takeaways.numbers: 100 samples/sec gives <1% CPU overhead and ~4MB memory overhead

takeaways.technique: Correlate resource metrics with workload timelines
takeaways.what_they_do: Correlate GPU utilization dips with CPU stack traces over the same time window to find what starves the accelerator.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can see the utilization drop down and that might be something that we want to investigate

takeaways.technique: Measure idle vs busy to right-size capacity
takeaways.what_they_do: Track per-process and node-level utilization to see when resources are underused and act on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we um improve our um software by like 10%, we might be able to just like turn off 10% of our like servers
